cards.explanation: The answer is water, friends. The text says the water was plentiful at Aenon near Salim, and people kept coming to be baptized. That's the reason John is there. I pick my bakery spot the same way, right next to the oven.

The answer is False. The text says John had not yet been thrown into prison. So John is still free and still out baptizing while this scene plays out. It's a quick note, but it tells everyone where we are on the timeline.

The dispute is about ceremonial washing, friends. A dispute arose between John's disciples and a certain Jew over the issue of ceremonial washing. The text doesn't tell us who said what in the argument. It only names the topic, and that topic leads straight to the disciples going to John.

The people are described this way: “…everyone is going to Him.” That's what John's disciples tell him, and they're talking about the One John testified about. I think those disciples sound a little rattled, but that's my guess, not the text. What matters is how John answers.

The first thing John says back is, “A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.” He doesn't argue about the crowds or count heads. He starts with what is given from heaven. I could use that instinct the next time my batch doesn't rise.

The answer is False. John doesn't say he is the Christ. He tells his disciples, “You yourselves can testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but am sent ahead of Him.’” He's reminding them of something they already heard from him, that he was sent ahead.

The answer is overjoyed, friends. John says the friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him, and is overjoyed to hear the bridegroom's voice. That's a happy kind of waiting, like hearing a loved one's key in the door. The friend is glad to hear that voice.

The answer is True, and it's John's own joy he's talking about. He says, “That joy is mine, and it is now complete.” He's the friend who stands and listens, and he takes the joy as his own. Nothing in what he says is missing.

John sums it up this way: “He must increase; I must decrease.” That's where his answer to his disciples lands, after he begins with “A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.” He's the friend of the bridegroom, and he's glad to see the bridegroom take center stage.

The answer is that He is above all, friends. John says, “The One who comes from heaven is above all.” He sets that next to the one from the earth, who belongs to the earth. Two kinds of speakers, and only one is above all.

The answer is False. John says the One from heaven testifies to what He has seen and heard, “…yet no one accepts His testimony.” That's the opposite of everyone accepting it. It's a heavy line, so I'll let it sit.

The person has certified that God is truthful, friends. John says, “Whoever accepts His testimony has certified that God is truthful.” Certified means signed and sealed, like a stamp of approval. The person who accepts the testimony puts that stamp on it, and the stamp says God is truthful.
The One whom God has sent is the one who speaks God's words. John says, “For the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God…” That's the same One from heaven he's been describing, friends.

The answer is False. John says, “The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.” All things, with nothing held back. The statement is simple and complete, so "only some" doesn't fit.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, friends. John says, “Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life.” Notice it's has, right now. It's a big promise in a short sentence.

The answer is True. John says whoever rejects the Son will not see life, and “Instead, the wrath of God remains on him.” This is a heavy part, and I won't joke about it. John says it right after the promise of eternal life.
